In [[geometry]], the '''gyroelongated cupolae''' are an infinite set of polyhedra, constructed by adjoining an ''n''-gonal [[cupola (geometry)|cupola]] to a 2''n''-gonal [[antiprism]].

There are three ''gyroelongated cupolae'' that are [[Johnson solid]]s made from regular triangles, squares, and pentagons. Higher forms can be constructed with isosceles triangles. Adjoining a [[triangular prism]] to a [[square antiprism]] also generates a polyhedron, but has adjacent parallel faces, so is not a Johnson solid. The hexagonal form can be constructed from regular polygons, but the cupola faces are all in the same plane. Topologically other forms can be constructed without regular faces.
